$Comment: The Headless Horseman's hard graveyard, the hard ride: the twin of Hallows_Eve_Graveyard.json
beside this file, with his hard fight in it. Every area of a copy pastes
Hallows_Eve/Hallows_Eve_Graveyard_Hard.prefab.json, the same night graveyard with his hard fight's
entity, his hard spawn marker and a way-out pad in its entrance room (tools/arena_markers.py writes
it from tools/arenas/Hallows_Eve_Graveyard_Hard.json), so every fresh paste stages a fresh hard
fight. EntryOffset lands an arriving party one block up, standing on the entrance room's floor, and
EntryYaw 180 turns them to face south, into the graveyard, away from the back wall and its way-out pad.
IntroCamera plays the normal graveyard's sweep, Hallows_Eve_Graveyard_Intro, since both share one
layout: each arriving player watches it with their movement held until the view is back.
Whoever opens this dungeon decides who may enter it; the file names no quest the player must have
done, so it stays free of any quest. Season keeps it closed outside Hallow's Eve. Share: one party
to an area, up to five players, and four areas to a copy. Complete names his hard fight, the script its prefab
runs, so the run clears when he falls, and Rewards rolls Hallows_Eve_Graveyard_Clear_Hard for each
member present as a Claim: full the first hard clear each day, half on later ones. Difficulty
files its runs and their returns under Hard, apart from the normal graveyard's. Text names it in
the reader's language (hallowseve.world.lang), and its GoalKey is the line each player reads as
they arrive.
EntryCost is the price of the hard ride: one Burning Grave Candle (Old Jack sells them at his
stall once he counts the player a Regular, or trades one for ten Grave Candles), taken from
whoever opens an area for their party;
partymates who follow into that fight walk in free. Confirm is left out, so it is on: before
anything is spent, the player opening the area sees CommonLib's confirm screen, built like the
game's portal summon screen, with the graveyard's name and description, the candle, how many they
hold and how many it takes, and a button whose words are ConfirmKey's ("Light the Candle"); it
burns the candle, sends the party in and plays the game's portal sound and sparkle, and closing the
screen spends nothing. With none, the button is off and the HintKey line says where to buy them.
Change Count to change the price, and the Gravekeeper's hard-ride label, which shows it, with it.
